faqs: How much does AI consulting cost per hour?

Upwork says AI consultants there generally charge $35 to $60 an hour, with the most experienced at $100 or more. On the US government's GSA schedule, the median ceiling rate for labor categories named "AI consultant" was $187.42 an hour on November 23, 2026, with a range of $123.24 to $300.82.
How much does it cost to hire an AI consultant for a project?

Upwork lists typical project prices of $1,500 to $4,000 for an AI readiness audit, $4,000 to $10,000 for a strategy and roadmap, $8,000 to $20,000 for a proof of concept, and $3,000 to $12,000 for ongoing advisory and deployment.
Is an AI consultant cheaper than hiring a data scientist?

It depends on the source. The 2025 median data scientist wage was $57.80 an hour, about $83 with benefits at the private-industry average. The GSA median AI consultant ceiling of $187.42 is far higher, while Upwork's typical $35 to $60 is lower. In our view a consultant makes sense for weeks of work, not a full-time role.
How much should I charge for AI consulting?

Public benchmarks run from the $35 to $60 an hour Upwork says is typical for its AI consultants to a $187.42 median ceiling for AI consultant categories on the GSA schedule. Experience matters: DXC Public Solutions' GSA ceilings run from $123.24 for its Junior AI Consultant (one year) to $215.55 for its Senior AI Consultant (ten years).
Do big consulting firms publish their AI consulting rates?

We could not find a published AI consulting rate card from the large strategy and accounting firms. The GSA ceiling rate tool does publish vendors' maximum hourly rates under their federal contracts, which are not the price on every order.
What should an AI consulting engagement deliver?

Deliverables in writing (a roadmap, prototype or running system), clear ownership of the code and accounts, and a monthly running cost estimate. NIST's AI Risk Management Framework, with its Govern, Map, Measure and Manage functions, is a free checklist for scope.
body:
Short answer. Upwork says AI consultants on its marketplace generally charge $35 to $60 an hour, with the most experienced at $100 or more, and fixed projects there run from $1,500 for a readiness audit to $20,000 for a proof of concept. Established IT vendors' government ceiling rates are higher: the median ceiling rate for labor categories named "AI consultant" on the US government's GSA schedule was $187.42 an hour on November 23, 2026, and the highest was $300.82.

Those are the public numbers. We could not find a published rate card from the large consultancies, and the ranges in the top search results for this question come from consultancies' own blogs. This guide uses rate data a buyer can check: marketplace pages, the GSA's awarded ceiling rates, and Bureau of Labor Statistics wages for the people who do the work. If you would rather have the automation built than advised on, see our AI automation agency page.

Sources were read on November 23, 2026. Every worked total below is our own arithmetic on those published numbers.

What an AI consultant does for a small business

An AI consultant helps you decide where AI is worth using, then plans or builds the first version. Upwork's own hiring page splits the work into four kinds of engagement, and they are a useful map of what you are buying:

  • Readiness audit. A review of your data and infrastructure, a shortlist of use cases and a readiness scorecard.
  • Strategy and roadmap. Prioritized use cases, an implementation roadmap, and a budget and KPI plan.
  • Proof of concept. A working prototype, a model evaluation and a recommendation on whether to deploy.
  • Ongoing advisory and deployment. Model fine tuning, performance monitoring and team training.

In our view, the most useful first output for a small business is narrow: one process that runs faster or costs less, such as answering missed calls, sorting inbound leads or drafting quotes. Our guide to AI implementation covers the steps after the plan, and the one on business process automation covers what to automate first.

AI consulting rates per hour: what public data shows

Three kinds of public source give hourly rates, and they measure different things.

SourceWho it coversHourly rate
UpworkFreelance AI consultants on its marketplace$35 to $60 generally; $100 or more for the most experienced
FiverrAI experts on its marketplace$40 to $200; $10 to $125 for AI strategy consultants
GSA schedule, "ai consultant"6 labor categories from 2 IT vendors (DXC Public Solutions, NU Info Systems)$123.24 to $300.82 ceiling; median $187.42
GSA schedule, "artificial intelligence"185 labor categoriesMedian $193.60 ceiling; middle half $142.00 to $258.18

Marketplace rates. Upwork says hiring an AI consultant there "generally ranges from $35-$60 per hour, similar to AI engineers, with the most experienced consultants charging $100 per hour or more." Fiverr's 2026 guide puts AI experts at $40 to $200 an hour and AI strategy consultants at $10 to $125. Both companies run the marketplaces they describe, so they have a stake in these numbers.

Government ceiling rates. The GSA's labor ceiling rate tool lists "fully burdened Not-to-Exceed Ceiling Rates awarded under GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contracts." A search for "ai consultant" on November 23, 2026 returned six categories: DXC Public Solutions' Junior AI Consultant at $123.24 an hour (one year of experience) up to its Senior AI Consultant at $215.55 (ten years), plus an IT AI Consultant at $300.82 from NU Info Systems. These are fully burdened maximums a vendor may charge federal buyers under that contract, not what every order pays. They are still the closest thing to a published rate card for an established IT firm.

We could not find a published AI consulting rate card from the large strategy and accounting firms. When a search result quotes a range for them, ask where it came from.

What AI consulting projects cost

Upwork also publishes typical project prices for the four engagement types above:

EngagementTypical price on UpworkLevelWhat you get
AI readiness audit$1,500 to $4,000Entry to intermediateData and infrastructure review, use case shortlist, readiness scorecard
AI strategy and roadmap$4,000 to $10,000Intermediate to expertPrioritized use cases, roadmap, budget and KPI plan
Proof of concept build$8,000 to $20,000ExpertWorking prototype, model evaluation, deployment recommendation
Ongoing advisory and deployment$3,000 to $12,000ExpertFine tuning, monitoring, team training

At the small end, Fiverr reports fixed project prices averaging $116.32 for strategic consulting and about $98.01 for AI lessons and training. At those prices, we would expect a session rather than a full plan.

The consulting fee is rarely the whole bill. A build also runs on software with its own meter: model API tokens, an automation platform, a phone number for a voice agent. Our AI model API pricing comparison and the guide to AI agent pricing show those running costs, and the AI chatbot for business cost guide works one example through.

AI consultant vs hiring an employee

The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes pay for the occupations closest to the work. The 2025 median pay was $48.97 an hour for management analysts (who, in the BLS description, "recommend ways to improve an organization's efficiency"), $57.80 for data scientists and $67.45 for computer and information research scientists.

A wage is not what an employee costs you. In the BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation release for June 2026, wages and salaries "accounted for 70.0 percent of employer costs" for private industry workers, and benefits the other 30.0 percent. If benefits ran at that average, a data scientist at the median would cost about $83 an hour worked ($57.80 divided by 0.70), or about $172,000 a year. That is our approximation: the 70 percent is an average across all private industry jobs, not a figure for data scientists.

OptionHourly cost160 hours (about one full-time month, our assumption)
Upwork freelancer, top of the typical range$60$9,600
Employed data scientist, wage plus average benefitsabout $83about $13,211
GSA "ai consultant" median ceiling$187.42$29,987

The consultant costs more per hour, about 2.3 times the employee at the GSA median, but a consultant is usually paid only for the agreed hours or project, not a salary that continues. We would hire when the AI work is continuous and central to the business, and use a consultant to find out whether it is.

A worked budget for a first AI project

Here is a hypothetical small business that wants an AI assistant to answer and sort inbound leads, priced from the public numbers above:

  1. Assessment, 20 hours. $700 to $1,200 at Upwork's typical $35 to $60 an hour; $3,748.40 at the GSA median ceiling of $187.42. Upwork's own readiness audit range is $1,500 to $4,000.
  2. Proof of concept. $8,000 to $20,000 at Upwork's typical project prices.
  3. Running costs. The software and API meter, priced separately (see the pricing guides linked above).

Using Upwork's project prices instead (the $1,500 audit floor plus the $8,000 proof of concept floor), a first project with an assessment and a working prototype starts around $9,500, before software. A one-week, 40-hour engagement at the GSA median ceiling would be $7,496.80. Your quotes will differ; the point is to know which tier a quote sits in.

What you should get for the money

A useful benchmark for scope is the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, released on January 26, 2023 and "intended for voluntary use." NIST says it is being revised under the White House AI Action Plan. Its playbook organizes the work into four functions, Govern, Map, Measure and Manage. In our plain reading, a good consultant's plan should touch each one:

  • Govern. Who owns the AI system, which data it may touch, and who signs off.
  • Map. Which process it changes, who it affects and what could go wrong.
  • Measure. How you will test accuracy and track results against a baseline.
  • Manage. What happens when it fails, and how it is monitored after launch.

Before you sign, we suggest asking for three things in writing: the deliverables (a roadmap, a prototype or a running system), who owns the code, prompts and accounts afterwards, and an estimate of the monthly running cost once the consultant leaves. A quote without the last one is incomplete.
